status_summary: H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) set new immigration fees, and a USCIS interim final rule published 2026-04-29 (effective 2026-05-29) codifies a minimum 100 dollar asylum application fee, a 100 dollar annual fee while an asylum application is pending, and a rule that these fees cannot be waived or reduced; the fees adjust for inflation each fiscal year, with FY2027 amounts published 2026-10-01. A court in Maryland stayed the annual asylum fee guidance on 2025-10-30 and lifted the stay on 2026-02-02, and that case is ongoing. A rule published 2026-01-12 raised premium processing fees by 5.72 percent for inflation from 2026-03-01 without adding forms, and a proposal of 2026-06-23 would raise the naturalization fee and end fee waivers and the reduced fee for it. A comprehensive USCIS fee rule raising all fees was not found.

timeline.event: H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21) was signed, setting new immigration fees including an asylum application fee and an annual fee while an asylum application is pending, with no waivers or reductions and yearly inflation adjustment.
timeline.source: Federal Register (USCIS interim final rule describing the law)

timeline.event: DHS announced it would begin collecting the 1,000 dollar parole fee required by H.R. 1.
The District of Maryland temporarily stayed USCIS and EOIR guidance on collecting the annual asylum fee in Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project v. USCIS.
DHS published FY2026 inflation adjustments for certain H.R. 1 fees (parole, ESTA, EVUS).
DHS published a rule raising premium processing fees for inflation, effective 2026-03-01; it did not add forms or classifications.
The court lifted its stay and denied a new temporary restraining order and injunction request on the annual asylum fee.
USCIS published an interim final rule (effective 2026-05-29) codifying H.R. 1 fees, including the asylum application fee, the annual asylum fee and no waivers or reductions for them.

USCIS proposed raising the naturalization application fee (Form N-400 from 760 to 1,330 dollars on paper) and ending the reduced fee and fee waivers for Forms N-400 and N-336, keeping the statutory exemption for military members; comments closed 2026-08-24.
USCIS published FY2027 inflation adjustments to H.R. 1 immigration fees, effective 2026-10-16, raising the annual asylum fee to 105 dollars and leaving the initial asylum fee at 100 dollars.

title: Raise USCIS fees, limit waivers, add an asylum fee, expand premium processing
uncertainties: The interim final rule was read in large part, but the amounts of some H.R. 1 fees (parole, special immigrant juvenile, TPS work permits) were taken from the FY2027 notice rather than the rule. The Clearinghouse page shows no docket entries after 2026-02-20, so later rulings, including on a pending motion to dismiss, are unknown. A 2024 USCIS fee rule predates the period and was not reviewed. The Mandate's request for fees tied to cost is only partly matched because the fees found are statutory minimums, inflation adjustments and one proposed naturalization fee increase. Progress was lowered from 55 to 45 because the general fee increase and the waiver limits beyond H.R. 1 fees are only proposed and premium processing was not expanded.
